result.title: An Input-Dependent Readout Phase for Resonant Sequence Models
result.summary: Sequence models with a fixed-size state avoid the quadratic cost of attention, but face a design choice. An input-dependent state transition gives content-dependent memory at the cost of FFT-based training, while a fixed transition keeps the O(T log T) convolutional path but reads memory the same way for every input. ResonatorLM, a recent model of the second kind, reads a bank of damped complex oscillators through a fixed learned phase per head. We make that readout phase a function of the current token, which adds input dependence to the read only, keeps the convolution exact, and costs 0.2 percent more parameters. An analysis of the untrained bank shows that phase does encode elapsed time, but an ordinary token falls below the background within 2-8 steps and no choice of damping extends linear reconstruction beyond about 16 tokens. In 6M-parameter character-level models on WikiText-2, the input-dependent phase matches the original at the training length and removes its failure beyond it: trained on 256 tokens and tested on 1024, perplexity falls from 12.81 to 3.76. We trace the failure to long-memory heads that accumulate more history than training exposed them to. The learned phase tracks the current character rather than distance and does not improve retrieval.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文把 ResonatorLM 中固定学习的读出相位改成当前 token 的函数，只在读出端引入输入依赖性，保持精确卷积且仅增 0.2% 参数；并分析无训练振荡器 bank 的时间编码能力，在 WikiText-2 字符级模型上验证其可消除超出训练长度的性能崩溃。
AI.relevance_reason: 固定状态递归加输入依赖读出的设计，以及训练长度 256、测试 1024 时的长度泛化失败诊断，可能为 LVR 的 latent 状态读取方式与长度泛化提供核查线索；文中读出相位追踪当前字符而非距离，也提示位置与内容解耦时可能的信息坍缩风险。
